applicable_when: B is declared with strides=(1, 512) and order=(0,1) — this is column-major layout where K is contiguous in global memory but N has stride 512. When Triton stages BLOCK_K×BLOCK_N=64×64 tiles of B through shared memory with order=(0,1), the N-stride of 512 floats maps multiple threads to the same shared memory bank (512 mod 32 = 0), causing 12-way bank conflicts on 77.65% of all shared load wavefronts. Changing B_block_ptr order to (1,0) makes Triton lay out the tile with N as the fast (innermost) dimension in shared memory, so consecutive threads access consecutive N-elements at stride-1 in shared memory — eliminating bank conflicts. Simultaneously, reducing BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K from 64 to 32 cuts the accumulator register footprint from 4096 to 1024 FP32 values, reducing registers/thread from 128 to ~64, which raises block_limit_shared_mem from 3 to ~6 blocks/SM and doubles theoretical occupancy. The grid grows from 93 to 310 blocks, covering all 132 SMs with 2.3 waves.
